report.currency: MYR (RM) — tables in RM millions, USD equivalents in parentheses at ~RM4.12/US$
report.verdict: A top-line quarter bought with margin. The first full quarter of commercial casino (live-table) operations at Resorts World New York City lifted Q3-26 group revenue 29.1% YoY to RM4.34bn (~US$1.05bn), but RWNYC ramp-up staffing costs, a 22% EBITDA decline at the Resorts World Genting cash cow and higher financing/transaction costs cut group adjusted EBITDA 11.3% to RM743.1m (~US$180m) and attributable profit 66% to RM40.6m (~US$10m). The New York ramp thesis is intact but is landing later and costlier than the Street modelled (US & Bahamas EBITDA RM200.5m vs Maybank's RM300m); the home-market decline is the bigger structural problem.
summary: **Revenue delivered the shape, not the margin.** Q3-26 group revenue rose 29.1% YoY to RM4.34bn (~US$1.05bn), which management attributed to the first full-quarter contribution from the initial phase of commercial casino operations at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC). Prior-year base implied by the reported growth rate is ~RM3.36bn (~US$816m).

**Adjusted EBITDA fell 11.3% to RM743.1m (~US$180m)** against an implied ~RM838m (~US$203m) a year ago; implied group margin compressed c.780bps to ~17.1% from ~24.9% (our arithmetic from reported growth rates — the filing's absolute comparatives were not readable in-session).

**Bottom line collapsed on cost and financing.** Profit attributable to shareholders was RM40.6m (~US$10m), down 66% from RM119.7m (~US$29m) in Q3-25 and down 14% QoQ from RM47.4m (~US$12m) in Q2-26. PBT fell 69% to RM80.2m (~US$19m). Attributable net margin is below 1% of revenue.

**The earnings miss sits in New York operating costs, not demand.** US & Bahamas adjusted EBITDA of RM200.5m (~US$49m), +33% YoY, landed ~RM100m (33%) below Maybank's RM300m (~US$73m) estimate and below consensus; the broker attributes the shortfall to higher RWNYC staff costs as the property continues to add gaming capacity.

**US & Bahamas is now the largest revenue segment.** Segment revenue +161% YoY to RM2.02bn (~US$490m) — 47% of group — but implied segment margin was only ~9.9% versus ~19.5% a year earlier (~RM151m EBITDA on ~RM774m revenue), i.e. the ramp is running with sharply negative operating leverage for now.

**Home market is the structural worry.** Malaysia (Resorts World Genting) revenue fell 14% to RM1.72bn (~US$417m) and adjusted EBITDA fell 22% to RM486.4m (~US$118m), on weaker gaming activity, lower visitation and higher operating costs. RWG still contributes ~65% of group EBITDA, so its ~RM137m YoY EBITDA decline more than offset the ~RM50m YoY gain from the US.

**Residual segments (UK & Egypt, Property, Investments & Others)** imply ~RM600m (~US$146m) of revenue and ~RM56m (~US$14m) of adjusted EBITDA by subtraction from group totals; the filing's segment-level split for these was not captured and is marked n/a.

**Capital structure reset in New York.** The group has put in place a new US$2.0bn secured credit facility at Genting Americas Inc to refinance Genting New York LLC's existing senior secured facility, redeem associate Empire Resorts' US$300.0m 7.75% senior secured notes, and support development and operation of the RWNYC commercial casino. Transaction costs for the facility were booked in Q3-26 (one-off).

**Financing costs are now a stated drag.** Management cited higher financing costs alongside higher operating costs as reasons for the profit decline — the direction of leverage is up as the RWNYC build-out is debt-funded. Net debt and cash balances at 30 Sep 2026 were not captured [unverified].

**No numeric guidance; qualitative priorities only.** Management says it is focused on rolling out RWNYC's premium gaming segment and driving revenue growth from full commercial casino operations, with operational and marketing synergies between RWNYC and Resorts World Catskills expected to support long-term growth of the New York operations.

**Sell-side has trimmed.** Post-results notes trimmed the outlook on costs and lower RWG visitors; Maybank expects earnings to 'improve markedly' in 1H27 as RWNYC table games ramp, but is less constructive on the home market, while still calling the shares deep value.

**Parent-level stress adds overhang.** Genting Bhd (GENM's controlling shareholder) swung to a RM161.4m (~US$39m) Q3 net loss on revenue +7.3% to RM8.02bn (~US$1.95bn), with its Singapore and Malaysia businesses cited as drags; Genting Bhd shares fell to a 20-year low on 27 Nov.

**No cost-transformation programme disclosed.** Unlike peers running explicit savings programmes, the captured disclosure contains no quantified cost-mitigation plan for RWG or RWNYC; cost pressure is being absorbed, not offset.

**No group event effect to quantify.** Q3-26 had no World Cup/major-event driver; the revenue swing is entirely structural (RWNYC licence conversion) and cyclical (RWG demand). Reported vs organic/FX split was not disclosed in captured sources.

**Dividend: none captured for Q3** [unverified]. GENM has historically paid interim dividends with H1 and final/special with Q4; a Q3 declaration would be unusual but we could not confirm the filing's dividend note.

**Thesis read-through:** the bull case (RWNYC full-casino economics) is visible in revenue but its margin proof is deferred to 1H27; the bear case (RWG demand/cost erosion, rising leverage, parent overhang) is showing up in the P&L now. Until RWNYC segment margin recovers toward the mid-teens and RWG stabilises, group EBITDA is likely to run below prior-year levels.

**Data caveat.** The primary Bursa filing and company press release could not be read in-session (fetch tooling capped); every headline figure above is corroborated across at least three outlets quoting the 26 Nov 2026 filing (Asia Gaming Brief, GGRAsia, Intergame; PBT via Minichart; Q2 PAT via Moomoo). Items marked n/a were not independently verified.

segments.name: Leisure & Hospitality – Malaysia (Resorts World Genting)
segments.headline: Revenue -14%, adj. EBITDA -22%: the monopoly cash cow is shrinking on demand and cost at the same time, and it still carries two-thirds of group EBITDA.
narrative: They reported Malaysia leisure and hospitality revenue down 14% year-on-year to RM1.72bn (~US$417m) and adjusted EBITDA down 22% to RM486.4m (~US$118m). Working back from the stated growth rates, the prior-year base was roughly RM2.0bn (~US$485m) of revenue and ~RM624m (~US$151m) of EBITDA, so segment margin compressed by about 290bps to ~28.3%. The segment remains ~65% of group adjusted EBITDA, which means the ~RM137m (~US$33m) year-on-year EBITDA decline here was larger than the entire ~RM50m (~US$12m) gain delivered by the US segment — the group result was decided at Resorts World Genting, not in Queens.

The drivers management cited, as relayed by the filing coverage, were weaker gaming activity, lower visitation and higher operating costs. The captured disclosure did not give VIP versus mass volumes, hold percentage, visitor arrivals, hotel occupancy or the gaming/non-gaming split, so we cannot say how much of the 14% revenue fall is volume versus luck — those lines are n/a for this note. The cost commentary continues the pattern seen through 2025–26 (higher labour and indirect-tax costs in Malaysia are background context rather than Q3 filing content), and with no quantified cost programme disclosed, the operating leverage is running the wrong way: a 14% revenue decline became a 22% EBITDA decline.

Because RWG is Malaysia's sole licensed casino, the decline cannot be read as share loss; it is demand and mix. That is worse, not better, for the thesis, because it implies the premium-player and regional-visitor base is softer and the fix is not a marketing-share battle but a macro/visitation recovery. Post-results broker notes trimmed outlooks specifically on costs and lower visitors, and Maybank described the home-market outlook as less sunny than New York. Management's own commentary, by contrast, was overwhelmingly about RWNYC — the RWG deterioration was explained but not addressed with a plan.

Our read for Q4-26: seasonality (year-end holidays) should lift RWG sequentially, but a return to year-on-year growth looks unlikely before comparatives ease in 2H27. The items we most want in the Q4 filing are visitor arrivals, hotel occupancy, and any statement on cost actions; absent those, we would model Malaysia EBITDA down high-teens year-on-year for FY26 (estimate) and treat the segment as the swing factor for group leverage, since it funds the New York capex.

segments.name: Leisure & Hospitality – US & Bahamas (RWNYC, Resorts World Catskills via Empire associate, Resorts World Bimini)
segments.headline: Revenue +161% on the first full quarter of commercial casino operations, but EBITDA +33% to RM200.5m was a third below the Street as table-game staffing front-ran revenue.
narrative: They reported US and Bahamas revenue up 161% year-on-year to RM2.02bn (~US$490m) and adjusted EBITDA up 33% to RM200.5m (~US$49m), with the quarter described as the first full-quarter contribution from the initial phase of commercial casino operations at Resorts World New York City. The implied prior-year base is ~RM774m (~US$188m) of revenue and ~RM151m (~US$37m) of EBITDA, so segment margin fell to ~9.9% from ~19.5% — a near-1,000bps compression that is the single largest reason group margin fell ~780bps. The segment is now 47% of group revenue but only ~27% of group EBITDA.

Management said the revenue gain was 'partially offset by higher ramp up costs associated with the commercial casino' as the property continues to add gaming capacity. Maybank had modelled RM300m (~US$73m) of US EBITDA on the first full quarter of tables; the ~RM100m (~US$24m) shortfall — attributed to higher RWNYC staff costs — accounts for essentially the whole group miss versus consensus. This is the known shape of a VLT-to-full-casino conversion: live tables are labour-intensive relative to electronic gaming, dealer and surveillance headcount is hired and trained ahead of the premium-segment launch, and the revenue per table matures over several quarters. The question is duration, not direction; the filing did not disclose RWNYC GGR, table count, slot/ETG count, hold or win per unit, so the productivity curve is n/a from the company and must be tracked via New York State Gaming Commission monthly data.

Strategically, management's priorities are the rollout of RWNYC's premium gaming segment and driving revenue from full commercial operations, with operational and marketing synergies between RWNYC and Resorts World Catskills expected to support long-term growth. The capital structure has been reorganised to match: a new US$2.0bn (~RM8.2bn) secured credit facility at Genting Americas Inc refinances Genting New York LLC's existing senior secured facility, redeems associate Empire Resorts' US$300.0m (~RM1.24bn) of 7.75% senior secured notes, and funds RWNYC development. Transaction costs for the facility were expensed in Q3 (one-off), but the higher gross debt is structural, and management explicitly flagged higher financing costs as a drag on profit.

Our judgement: the ramp is real but the Street's margin timing was too aggressive. Maybank now expects earnings to 'improve markedly' in 1H27 as table games mature; we would model US segment margin recovering toward the mid-teens through 1H27 (estimate) as revenue outgrows a largely fixed labour base, with the premium-segment launch the key catalyst. Resorts World Bimini and the Catskills contribution were not separately disclosed (n/a). Watch monthly RWNYC GGR, the redemption and refinancing close, and any disclosure on premium-segment opening timing.

segments.name: UK & Egypt, Property, Investments & Others (residual)
segments.headline: Not disclosed in captured sources; by subtraction the remaining segments contributed ~RM600m of revenue and ~RM56m of adjusted EBITDA.
narrative: The captured coverage of the 26 Nov 2026 filing did not break out the United Kingdom and Egypt leisure and hospitality segment (Genting Casinos UK, Crockfords Cairo), the Property segment or Investments and Others. Subtracting the Malaysia and US and Bahamas figures from the group totals leaves ~RM600m (~US$146m) of revenue and ~RM56m (~US$14m) of adjusted EBITDA across these lines. Because Investments and Others typically carries central costs and can be negative, the standalone UK and Egypt EBITDA is likely higher than the residual suggests, but we cannot verify this and mark the segment detail n/a.

On the residual arithmetic, the combined margin of these segments is roughly 9%, which would be consistent with a UK land-based casino business running thin margins, but we flag that this is an inference, not a disclosure. Year-on-year movements, constant-currency growth and any GBP translation effect are n/a.

Nothing in the captured management commentary referenced the UK estate, Egypt or property sales, which suggests they were not material swing factors in the quarter; management's narrative was concentrated on RWNYC and RWG. We would nonetheless want the Q4 filing to confirm UK and Egypt EBITDA trajectory, given UK regulatory cost pressure across the land-based sector.

Watch items: UK and Egypt segment EBITDA and any impairment commentary; Property segment land-sale timing; and whether the Investments and Others line absorbed any of the Genting Americas facility transaction costs (which would flatter the operating segments).

highlights.text: RWNYC's conversion to a full commercial casino is now in the numbers: US & Bahamas revenue +161% YoY to RM2.02bn (~US$490m) in the first full quarter of live-table operations, making it the largest revenue segment (47% of group).
US & Bahamas adjusted EBITDA still grew 33% YoY to RM200.5m (~US$49m) despite absorbing ramp-up staffing costs — the segment is accretive even in its least efficient phase.
Group revenue +29.1% YoY to RM4.34bn (~US$1.05bn) — the first step-change in the group's revenue base since the Malaysia monopoly matured.

New US$2.0bn (~RM8.2bn) Genting Americas secured credit facility consolidates the New York capital structure, refinances the GENNY facility and takes out Empire Resorts' 7.75% US$300m notes — should lower the blended coupon on the US debt stack once transaction costs wash through.
Premium gaming segment rollout at RWNYC is the next catalyst; management is explicitly prioritising it, and Maybank expects earnings to 'improve markedly' in 1H27 as tables mature.
The Q3 earnings hit includes one-off transaction costs for the new facility — part of the 66% attributable-profit decline is non-recurring.

lowlights.text: Resorts World Genting revenue -14% to RM1.72bn (~US$417m) and adjusted EBITDA -22% to RM486.4m (~US$118m) on weaker gaming activity, lower visitors and higher opex — a monopoly asset shrinking on demand and cost simultaneously, with no cost programme disclosed.
Group adjusted EBITDA -11.3% to RM743.1m (~US$180m) and implied margin c.-780bps to ~17.1%: revenue growth is currently dilutive.
US & Bahamas EBITDA of RM200.5m was ~RM100m (33%) below Maybank's RM300m and below consensus on higher RWNYC staff costs — the Street's ramp curve was too steep and estimates are being cut.
Attributable profit -66% YoY to RM40.6m (~US$10m) and -14% QoQ; PBT -69% to RM80.2m (~US$19m). Higher financing costs are now a stated structural drag as the RWNYC build is debt-funded.

Controlling shareholder Genting Bhd posted a RM161.4m (~US$39m) Q3 net loss and its shares hit a 20-year low on 27 Nov — group-level sentiment and potential capital-allocation pressure are an overhang.

Disclosure gaps: no RWNYC GGR/table metrics, no RWG visitor or hold data, no net debt/cash figure captured, no 9M figures captured — management is emphasising the New York narrative while the home-market deterioration and balance-sheet direction are under-explained.

forecast.intro: Genting Malaysia does not issue numeric guidance, so the 'bridge' is between Street expectations and delivery. The miss was entirely a US & Bahamas cost story: Maybank had RM300m (~US$73m) of segment EBITDA for the first full table-games quarter and got RM200.5m (~US$49m), with higher RWNYC staff costs the stated cause. Malaysia then compounded it, with EBITDA -22% YoY to RM486.4m (~US$118m) on lower visitors, weaker gaming activity and higher opex. Net: group adjusted EBITDA RM743.1m (~US$180m), -11.3% YoY, and attributable profit RM40.6m (~US$10m), -66%. Post-results, brokers trimmed outlooks on costs and lower visitors; Maybank's qualitative guide is for a marked improvement in 1H27 as RWNYC tables ramp, with the home market 'less sunny'. Management's own forward commentary is limited to prioritising the RWNYC premium-gaming rollout and Catskills synergies.

forecast.view: **Q4-26 (estimate):** we would model group revenue of ~RM4.4–4.6bn (~US$1.07–1.12bn) as RWNYC adds capacity and RWG gets its seasonal year-end lift, with group adjusted EBITDA of ~RM750–850m (~US$182–206m) — a US segment margin drifting toward low-double-digits and Malaysia still down year-on-year. **FY26:** group adjusted EBITDA is tracking below FY25 on our arithmetic, because the RWG decline (~RM137m in Q3 alone) outweighs the US ramp until table productivity normalises. **Margin:** the inflection is a 1H27 event — US segment margin recovering toward the mid-teens as revenue outgrows a largely fixed dealer/surveillance base, premium-segment launch the catalyst. **Leverage:** direction is up — the US$2.0bn (~RM8.2bn) Genting Americas facility, Empire note redemption and RWNYC capex all add gross debt while group EBITDA is falling; net debt/EBITDA (not captured) should be assumed to rise into 1H27 before improving. **Swing factors:** (1) RWNYC monthly GGR trajectory and the timing of premium-segment opening; (2) RWG visitor arrivals and whether management launches a cost programme; (3) interest cost after refinancing; (4) parent Genting Bhd's financial stress and any implications for GENM dividends. All figures in this paragraph are analyst estimates, not company guidance.
